MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 11, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell at
5:00 p.m., on July 11, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on July 6, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Labor Attorney Peter Brown: Employee
  Organization: Service Employees’ International Union (SEIU)

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Threat to Public Services or Facilities; Consultation with
  City Attorney and Director of Information Technology David Meyer

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  1  July 11, 2023
 At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:02 pm with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curly stated there was no reportable action on either Closed Session item.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim August 18, 2023 To Be Never Give Up Day

  Mayor Goodell announced proclamation .

P2. Proclaim Michael Block as a Hometown Hero

  Mayor Goodell presented proclamation to Michael Block.

P3. Recognize Mission Viejo Animal Services Volunteers

  Received presentation from Director Michelle Claud-Clemente and recognized the
  volunteers.

P4. Presentation by Santa Margarita Water District Board President Frank Ury

  Received presentation.

Cathy Schlicht, MV: Criticized Frank Ury and the City Council for the twelve-million-dollar
infrastructure improvements and education center for the water district that will be paid by the
taxpayers. She stated that there should have been a cost study that would have shown the cost savings
through a lease agreement versus a cost sharing agreement with the water district.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Walt Lawson, MV: Commended the City on Item #11 relating to the purchase of an electric vehicle
and referenced an LA Times article regarding the City of Laguna Beach and electric vehicles. He
spoke on various topics including the Los Oso project, the City’s Housing Element, the Oso Creek
trail and the cost of this project, and lastly, he spoke on the appeal case.

Sharon Genton, Lake Forest: The number of McKinney-Vento children has grown in Mission Viejo.
Spoke about an upcoming community event “Sole Support” which is collecting new tennis shoes for
these children in the City. She outlined the drop off locations that will accept donations through
August 7.

City Council Minutes  2  July 11, 2023
 Cathy Schlicht, MV: Stated that the City Attorney took her public comments from the June 23, 2020
meeting out of context to fit a false narrative that was submitted to the Court of Appeals. She spoke
out that item #14 should not be on the Consent Calendar and outlined out her reasons.

Michelle O’Brien, MV: Spoke on the Elks Lodge events and how they give back to the
community. She thanked both Mayor Goodell and Council Member Ruesch for attending the
recent Flag Day Ceremony.

Jill Schindler, MV: Questioned consent calendar item #10 regarding crossing guard services and
asked which school is losing a crossing guard.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items, 10, 11, and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of July 11, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated June 16, 2023 in the Amount of $1,495,418.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated June 23, 2023 in the Amount of $795,641.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated June 16, 2023 in the Amount of $2,176.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated June 23, 2023 in the Amount of $12,014.92

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2023

  Receive and file.
City Council Minutes  3  July 11, 2023
 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for May 2023

  Receive and file.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for May 2023

  Receive and file.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2023

  Receive and file.

12. Destruction of Records - Citywide Annual Records Purge

  Adopted Resolution 23-31 Authorizing and Directing the Community Relations Department
  to Destroy Certain City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State
  of California.

13. Amendment to Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and Processing Agreement

  (1) Approved the third amendment to the Agreement with Ingram Library Services, LLC for
  the period July 12, 2023 to June 30, 2024 in an amount not to exceed $150,000 for the provision
  of electronic selection lists, electronic ordering, acquisitions, cataloging, and physical
  processing of library materials; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Ingram
  Library Services, LLC for the period July 12, 2023 to June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed
  $150,000

15. 2023 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 24838)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer, and
  authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

16. 2023 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 24838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt, Inc. (A23-
  41) in the amount of $3,823,222.00.

17. Renewed Measure M (M2) Public Works Seven-Year Capital Improvement Program

  Adopted Resolution 23-30 Adopting a Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Capital
  Improvement Program (CIP), Beginning with the 2023/2024 Fiscal Year, to Satisfy the City's
  Eligibility Requirements of the Orange County Measure M (M2) Program.

City Council Minutes  4  July 11, 2023
 18. Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Received and filed.

19. Lower Curtis Park Land Exchange

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to execute a Land Exchange Agreement with the County of
  Orange (A23-42) to facilitate the creation of a graded pad below Curtis Park, and (2) authorized
  the City Manager to sign all quitclaim deeds and other supporting documents as may be
  required for the land exchange.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10. 2023-2025 School Crossing Guard Services

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1) award
  the contract in the amount of $1,102,087 to American Guard Services, Inc., (A23-39) for
  school crossing guard services for the period of August 1, 2023, to July 30, 2025; and (2)
  authorize issuance of a purchase order to American Guard Services, Inc., in an amount not to
  exceed $546,833 for the period of August 1, 2023, to July 30, 2024.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Purchase (1) Electric Vehicle - Replacement City Carpool Vehicle

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended the resourcefulness of City Staff on the purchase of this
  vehicle which will be funded by the forfeited C&D deposits.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Goodell, to (1) authorize the
  issuance of a Purchase Order for the purchase of a 2019 Chevrolet Bolt EV in the amount of
  $19,450.00, and (2) adopt Resolution 23-29 Amending the FY 2023/24 Operating Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  July 11, 2023
 14. Real Estate Advisory Services - Public Private Partnership for Los Osos (CAVP)
  Project

  Council Member Vasquez voiced concerns as to why a request for proposal was not issued on
  this project and why it was on the Consent Calendar.

  Cathy Schlicht, MV: Gave her opinions on the contract and she believes the end game is to
  create tax districts. She outlined the Scope of Service attached to the contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, approve the
  agreement with Kosmont Companies (A23-40) in the amount of $49,470 to provide
  professional services related to the identification and eventual selection of a retail development
  partner.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARING

20. Consideration of a Regular and an Urgency Ordinance, as an Uncodified Ordinance,
  Adopting Phase 1 Objective Design Standards, to Provide a Set of Clear, Objective, and
  Measurable Standards for Multi-Family Residential and Mixed-Use Projects to Ensure
  High Quality Design that Maintains the Architectural Character of Mission Viejo

  Director of Planning Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Mayor Goodell opened the Public Hearing at 7:30.

  Mayor Goodell closed the Public Hearing at 7:30 with no public comments.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  (1) find that the adoption of Objective Design Standards (ODS) is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15060, subd.
  ( c )(2), 15061, subd. (b )(3) and Section 15378 (b); (2) adopt Urgency Ordinance 23-350
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 36937(b) and Including the Facts Supporting the
  Urgency Declaration; and (3) introduced Ordinance 23-350A Adopting an Uncodified
  Regulatory Enactment Titled "Phase 1 Objective Design Standards and Ordering the
  Immediate Use and Reliance Upon these Objective Design Standards for all purpose.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  6  July 11, 2023
 OLD BUSINESS

21. Financial Feasibility and Funding Options Related to the Possible Construction and
  Operations of a Parking Structure Located in the Vicinity of the Oso Creek Golf Course
  and the Marguerite Recreation Center/Oso Creek Trail

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Troy Roelen, MV: Stated that he appreciates the Council’s vision on this project. He is in favor
  of this project.

  Jill Schindler, MV: Questioned the proposal and the dollar amount. She asked if this is for
  parking or more pickle ball courts.

  Cathy Schlicht, MV: Expressed to the Council that they need to put a stop to this parking
  structure and stated this is a multi-million-dollar contract for PRES Companies and suggested
  that an investigation be conducted on the relationship between Mayor Goodell and PRES. She
  outlined her reasoning for this.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to award a
  contract to the PRES Companies (A23-43) in an amount of $71,000.00 to complete a
  preliminary financial analysis that would include the determination of the amount of private
  and/or public financing sources available to construct and operate a parking Structure in the
  vicinity of the Oso Creek Golf Course which is for the Phase I Scope of Work.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

22. Performing Arts Theater Feasibility and Market Study

  Direct of Library Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, MV: Criticized the City Attorney on his comments in regards to the Parking
  Structure discussion on item #21. Stated she is in support of the feasibility study for a theater
  and asked if the Council is serious in finding a home for the theater.

  Robert Breton, MV:  Pointed out his involvement in cultural arts throughout the City and
  recapped the Cultural Arts Master Plan which he was appointed to the steering committee
  seven years ago. He announced that the Play Hamlet will be performed on the Village Green
  next week.

  Josh Vecchione, MV: He agrees this is a fabulous Company to contract with and encouraged
  the Council to form a committee to work with the consultant.
City Council Minutes  7  July 11, 2023
   Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  award the contract for the subject services to TheatreDNA (A23-44) for the period July 12,
  2023 to June 30, 2024 in an amount not to exceed $89,500; and (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to TheatreDNA for the period July 12, 2023 to June 30, 2024, in an amount not
  to exceed $89,500.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

23. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2023 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Mayor Goodell appointed himself as voting delegate and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and Council
  Member Vasquez as alternates for the League of California Cities Conference Annual
  Business Meeting on Friday September 22, 2023.

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

24. City Representation at the Oceania National Olympic Committee’s (ONOC) Pacific
  Games and meetings in Solomon Islands

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Council Member Vasquez voiced her concerns regarding budget and taxpayer dollars being
  spent.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, approve
  Mayor Goodell to attend and represent the City at the Oceania National Olympic Committee's
  Pacific Games to be held in the Solomon Islands, November 19 - December 2, 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  July 11, 2023
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum gave a shout-out to North Mission Viejo Little League 10U and 12U
Allstars for their amazing run in the District 68 Championships. She announced that the next Sober
Living Task Force meeting will be this Friday July 14 at 2:00 pm at Laguna Niguel City Hall.
Council Member Bucknum gave an update on the Task Force. She attended Concert on the Green
and announced upcoming events at the Norman P. Community Center. Council Member Bucknum
gave kudos to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for the 4th of July Street Fair and fireworks
show. She mentioned that she is aware of the complaints about the expensive food trucks and perhaps
next year the Committee can find some less expensive options. She attended the SCCOR
Appreciation Luncheon to recognize the volunteers. She mentioned that the Oso Creek Golf Course
will be hosting a Family Links Staycation this Saturday at 3 pm which will provide events for the
whole family. Council Member Bucknum stated that Sunday is the Boot Beer& BBQ 4:00 pm at
the Norman P. Community Center that benefits the Adopted Marines Committee. She reminded
everyone that July 19, 7 to 8:30 pm is Shakespeare in the Park featuring Hamlet. She announced
that the Nadadores are hosting the 2023 USA Diving Junior Nationals Championships at the aquatics
center starting on July 23. Lastly, she reminded residents that the Pacific Symphony Prelude in the
Park on August 5. She wished everyone a happy Summer as the City Council will be dark until later
in August.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch indicated that he also attended the events that Council Member Bucknum
outlined. He stated that he attended the ACC-OC Smart City Quarterly Policy Dinner and the
Saddleback Place Ribbon Cutting Ceremony on July 6. Lastly, he announced he attended the
Moulton Niguel Water District Public Safety Appreciation Day.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the 4th of July Street Fair and fireworks and did agree that the
food trucks were a little pricey. She announced that her husband is turning 50 and they will be going
on a cruise. Lastly, she stated that there is six more weeks before the kids go back to school.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated she also attended the same events as Council Members Bucknum and
Ruesch. She announced that the Boots, Beer & Barbecue event is sold out. She thanked the Animal
Services Volunteers that were recognized this evening. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley highlighted the hard
City Council Minutes  9  July 11, 2023
 work the Mission Viejo Activity Members during the Fourth of July Street Faire and pointed out
that the Orange County Health Department has cracked down on the types of food booths. She
thanked the SCOR Volunteers as well.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that he appreciated all the vigorous discussions this evening and the actions
that were taken. He thanked staff that attended his mother’s Celebration of Life. He announced that
the Junior Nationals Diving Championships will start on Saturday July 22.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 9:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 22, 2023, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________
 Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 22, 2023

City Council Minutes  10  July 11, 2023
